educational_units.description: The four BI-RADS categories of breast density: (A) almost entirely fatty, (B) scattered areas of fibroglandular density, (C) heterogeneously dense, (D) extremely dense.
educational_units.title: Breast Density Categories

educational_units.description: Breast density is defined as the relative proportion of breast parenchyma to fat within the breast.
educational_units.title: Breast Density Definition

educational_units.description: Reporting breast density is required by FDA legislation as of September 2024, with specific language requirements for both referring physicians and patients.
educational_units.title: Reporting Requirements

educational_units.description: The evolution of breast density classification from percentage-based to likelihood-based assessment with BI-RADS 5th Edition and v2025.
educational_units.title: Density Classification Evolution

educational_units.description: Breast density can vary due to factors like weight changes, estrogen replacement therapy, menopause, etc.
educational_units.title: Factors Affecting Breast Density

educational_units.description: How breast density affects mammographic accuracy through the masking effect of dense fibroglandular tissue.
educational_units.title: Impact of Breast Density on Mammographic Accuracy

educational_units.description: Advances in technology (film-screen to digital mammography to DBT) that have reduced the masking effect of dense breast tissue.
educational_units.title: Technology Advances in Mammography

educational_units.description: The increased cancer detection rates with advanced technologies, particularly in women with dense breasts.
educational_units.title: Cancer Detection Rates

educational_units.description: How different breast density categories correlate with increased breast cancer risk (odds ratios provided).
educational_units.title: Breast Cancer Risk Associated with Density

educational_units.description: The characteristics of masses in mammography: shape (oval, lobulated, round, irregular), margin (circumscribed, obscured, indistinct, spiculated), and density (fat-containing, low, equal, high).
educational_units.title: Mass Characteristics

educational_units.description: The classification of calcifications into typically benign and suspicious morphology types, along with distribution patterns.
educational_units.title: Calcification Types

educational_units.description: Other findings categories including architectural distortion, asymmetries, lymph nodes, skin lesions, dilated ducts, associated features, special cases, and location of findings.
educational_units.title: Other Findings Categories

human_summary: This educational material covers the BI-RADS® Mammography Lexicon with a focus on breast density classification, reporting requirements, and clinical significance. The content includes detailed categorizations of breast tissue, findings (masses, calcifications, etc.), and the impact of breast density on mammographic accuracy and cancer risk. The material is well-structured with tables and figures illustrating each breast density category.
illustrations_note: The material includes 16 figures (Figures 1-16) that visually demonstrate each breast density category (A-D) with both mediolateral oblique (MLO) and craniocaudal (CC) views. These images are essential for visual learning and should be incorporated into interactive tasks that require image identification and classification.

not_recommended.reason: This material doesn't contain factual errors that would benefit from this type of detection exercise.

recommendations.rationale: Multiple choice questions effectively test recognition and recall of the four breast density categories, reporting requirements, cancer detection rates, and risk associations.
Open-ended questions allow students to demonstrate conceptual understanding of breast density definition and its impact on mammographic accuracy.
Sequence tasks are ideal for understanding the evolution of density classification, technological advances in mammography, and the hierarchical organization of mass characteristics.
Click text tasks effectively test identification of factors affecting breast density from a list that may include distractors.
Multiple choice questions can efficiently test knowledge of calcification types and other findings categories.
